problem: WebKit is listed as the current native library for web content. Android's WebView has been based on Chromium (Blink), not WebKit, since Android 4.4 (API 19). A student reading this in 2024+ gets an outdated fact.
fix: Say: 'the WebView engine for web content, which is Chromium-based on modern Android (it used WebKit before Android 4.4).'

problem: 'All three are written in the module's build.gradle ... Gradle copies them into the manifest' implies compileSdk also reaches the manifest. Only minSdk and targetSdk become manifest attributes; compileSdk is build-time only and never appears in the manifest.
fix: Say: 'minSdk and targetSdk are written in build.gradle and Gradle copies them into the manifest as minSdkVersion and targetSdkVersion. compileSdk is build-time only and is never put in the manifest.'

problem: The sentence 'ART replaced Dalvik from Android 5.0; it compiles ahead of time at install and just in time while the app runs' merges two eras. In Android 5.0 and 6.0 ART was ahead-of-time only at install; just-in-time compilation with profile-guided AOT arrived in Android 7.0.
fix: Say: 'ART replaced Dalvik from Android 5.0, compiling ahead of time at install. From Android 7.0 it also compiles just in time while the app runs, and later ahead-of-time compiles follow the recorded hot paths.'

problem: The guard 'if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 24)' is presented as the general rule, but the constant must be the API level that introduced the method being called, not a fixed 24.
fix: Say: 'each call to a method added after API 21 must be wrapped in a guard using that method's own API level, for example if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 26) for a method added in API 26'.

problem: 'baseline profiles, which record the hot code paths at install' is wrong about when they are made. Baseline profiles are generated at build time (from benchmark runs) and shipped inside the APK; ART uses them during installation to compile those paths ahead of time.
fix: Say: 'baseline profiles, which list the hot code paths and ship inside the APK so ART can compile them ahead of time at install, making start-up faster.'
